news.title: Dani Olmo accuses Argentina coach of 'lying' about World Cup final punch
news.lede: Spain star Dani Olmo has rubbished Roberto Ayala’s apology (Picture: Getty) Dani Olmo has dismissed Roberto Ayala’s apology after their altercation in the wake of the World Cup final and accused the Argentina coach of ‘lying’ with his version of events. Ferran Torres’ emphatic extra-time strike proved the difference as Spain overcame Argentina’s gamesmanship and questionable tactics to get their hands on the coveted prize for a second time in the nation’s history. However, violent clashes involving the two sets of players threatened to overshadow Spain’s celebrations after the final whistle, with Leandro Paredes pictured shoving and kicking Gavi and Eric Garcia. Meanwhile, in a separate skirmish, Lionel Scaloni’s assistant Ayala was seen raising his hands and seemingly punching Olmo in the neck area, sending the Barcelona star backwards with some force.

news.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino accuses critics of spreading hate at World Cup
news.lede: Infantino claims critics of World Cup ‘missed it all’. He again defends Balogun affair and treatment of Iran. The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has hit back at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives while defending the tournament ⁠as a success that celebrated ⁠unity, safety and inclusion. In ​an open letter published on Monday, Infantino said detractors had overlooked the joy and togetherness experienced by millions of fans around the world who witnessed the tournament, ⁠won by Spain and staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico.

news.title: Gianni Infantino’s rambling World Cup rant shows FIFA boss has gone ‘full Donald Trump’
news.lede: Considering the amount of personal criticism he gets, Gianni Infantino is allowed the right to respond. And the FIFA president can respond in whatever manner he sees fit. Had he responded via a press conference at the end of the World Cup, it might have been better. But if he wants to do it in a 15-slide post on social media, that is fine.

news.title: 'Not sorry at all' - Spain's Dani Olmo claims Argentina coach ‘not telling truth’ about punch after World Cup final
news.lede: DANI OLMO has snubbed Roberto Ayala’s apology after being struck by the Argentina coach at the World Cup. Ayala thrusting a hand towards Olmo’s throat was just one part of the melee that followed the final in New Jersey. The right-handed jab appeared to come from absolutely nowhere as players and staff from both sides clashed after Spain‘s 1-0 win in extra-time. Ayala, 53, claimed it was in response to Olmo mouthing off.

news.title: World Cup final referee Slavko Vincic quits football days later as statement released
news.lede: The Slovenian FA have confirmed that World Cup final referee Slavko Vincic has officially retired. The 46-year-old was selected by FIFA to officiate Spain's prestigious win over Argentina and has now chosen to end his career, as confirmed by the football association of his home country. The opening to their official statement read: "One week after the World Cup final in the USA, Slavko Vinčić officially concluded his historic refereeing career at the very top of the world. "The Maribor native became the first Slovenian head referee to officiate the grand final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, confirming his status as one of the greatest officials in history.

news.title: Over 23 Million Football Fans Sign Petition Calling For Argentina To Be Banned From World Cup
news.lede: Fans were left furious after the World Cup final. By Syazwan Bahri | 27 Jul 2026, 04:08 PM. The viral petition, titled Argentina Out, attracted 23.3 million signatures from supporters across roughly 170 countries within a single week. The petition closed after Spain secured a 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina in the final on 19 July.

news.title: World Cup 2026: Gianni Infantino tells Fifa critics to 'meditate, pray or watch football'
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been Fifa president since 2016. Fifa president Gianni Infantino has told critics to "meditate, pray or watch a football match" instead of "spreading hate and false rumours" about his leadership, the governing body and the World Cup. In a 15-slide post on his personal Instagram account - reposted to Fifa's eight million followers - Infantino addressed "those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens" to affirm his belief that, while they were "busy planting seeds of hate", Fifa was delivering the "greatest event on earth". He said the World Cup "celebrated humanity at its best", adding that the 2026 tournament had "100% safety and security, only joy and happiness".
